## The plan/execute split

A conventional warp pipeline reads source data and reprojects it in one step.
**rwarp** separates these into two explicit phases:

1. `warp_plan()` — pure geometry; no I/O. Returns the source windows and
   destination sub-windows needed. Inspect, cache, or parallelise this.
2. `warp_exec()` — the actual pixel work, driven by a user-supplied
   `read_fn` (or `warp_buffer()`, for a window you have already read).

This means you can:

- **Inspect fill ratios** before deciding whether to fetch data at all.
- **Cache plans** when the same destination grid is reused across many dates.
- **Swap the reader** between GDAL, HTTP byte-refs, Zarr, or in-memory buffers
  without touching the warp logic.
- **Parallelise** by distributing chunks across workers.

## Anatomy of a plan

```{r plan_structure}
library(rwarp)
library(vaster)

## A 10-degree-per-pixel global source
src_gt  <- c(-180, 10, 0, 90, 0, -10)   # 36 x 18 grid
src_dim <- c(36L, 18L)

## A Web Mercator destination at ~156 km/pixel (zoom 1)
dst_gt  <- c(-20037508, 156543, 0, 20037508, 0, -156543)
dst_dim <- c(256L, 256L)

plan <- warp_plan(
  src_crs  = "EPSG:4326", src_gt = src_gt, src_dim = src_dim,
  dst_crs  = "EPSG:3857", dst_gt = dst_gt,
  dst_off  = c(0L, 0L), dst_size = dst_dim
)

cat("Length of plan:", length(plan), "\n")
cat("Chunks in first group:", length(plan[[1]]), "\n")

ch <- plan[[1]][[1]]
cat("\nChunk fields:\n")
str(ch)
```

## Fill ratio

The fill ratio tells you what fraction of the destination window has a valid
source pixel.  Values below 1 indicate that the source does not fully cover
the destination.

```{r fill}
## A high-latitude destination that only partially overlaps the source
## (global geographic source, destination tile near the North Pole in LAEA)
src_gt2  <- c(-180, 1, 0, 90, 0, -1)
src_dim2 <- c(360L, 180L)

dst_gt2  <- c(-500000, 5000, 0, 500000, 0, -5000)   # 1000 km at North Pole
dst_dim2 <- c(200L, 200L)

plan2 <- warp_plan(
  src_crs  = "EPSG:4326",
  src_gt   = src_gt2,
  src_dim  = src_dim2,
  dst_crs  = "+proj=laea +lat_0=90 +datum=WGS84 +type=crs",
  dst_gt   = dst_gt2,
  dst_off  = c(0L, 0L), dst_size = dst_dim2
)

if (!is.null(plan2)) {
  cat("Fill ratio:", plan2[[1]][[1]]$fill_ratio, "\n")
} else {
  cat("No overlap (NULL plan)\n")
}
```

## Antimeridian splitting

A destination across the antimeridian of a global longitude/latitude
source needs source pixels at both of its edges, 180 W and 180 E. One
window holding both is a strip the whole width of the source, which is what
gdalwarp reads. `warp_plan()` instead splits the chunk where source x
jumps, so each side reads a compact window at its own edge
(`split_antimeridian = TRUE`, the default; `FALSE` is gdalwarp's plan).

```{r antimeridian}
## Lambert azimuthal equal-area centred on 30 S, 180 E, 4000 km across
pac_crs <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=-30 +lon_0=180 +datum=WGS84 +type=crs"
pac_gt  <- c(-2e6, 20000, 0, 2e6, 0, -20000)
glob_gt <- c(-180, 1, 0, 90, 0, -1)

plan3 <- warp_plan("EPSG:4326", glob_gt, c(360L, 180L), pac_crs, pac_gt,
                   dst_size = c(200L, 200L))
plan3_g <- warp_plan("EPSG:4326", glob_gt, c(360L, 180L), pac_crs, pac_gt,
                     dst_size = c(200L, 200L), split_antimeridian = FALSE)

windows <- function(p) do.call(rbind, lapply(p[[1]], as.data.frame))
w  <- windows(plan3)
wg <- windows(plan3_g)
w[c("dst_xoff", "dst_xsize", "src_xoff", "src_yoff", "src_xsize", "src_ysize")]
c(split = sum(w$src_xsize * w$src_ysize), one_window = sum(wg$src_xsize * wg$src_ysize))
```

The two halves of the destination each read 26 columns at one edge. The two
destination columns that straddle the jump are chunks of their own, reading
two columns at each edge. Together that's about a sixth of the pixels in the
full-width strip:

```{r antimeridian-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.9}
lon <- function(x) glob_gt[1] + x * glob_gt[2]
lat <- function(y) glob_gt[4] + y * glob_gt[6]
box <- function(d, ...) {
  rect(lon(d$src_xoff), lat(d$src_yoff + d$src_ysize),
       lon(d$src_xoff + d$src_xsize), lat(d$src_yoff), ...)
}
op <- par(mar = c(2.5, 2.5, 2, 0.5))
plot(NA, xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(-90, 90), asp = 1, xlab = "", ylab = "",
     main = "What each plan reads from the global source")
rect(-180, -90, 180, 90, border = "grey60")
abline(v = c(-180, 180), col = "grey60")
box(wg, border = "grey30", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
box(w, col = adjustcolor("firebrick", 0.45), border = "firebrick")
legend("top", c("split (default)", "one window (gdalwarp)"), horiz = TRUE,
       col = c("firebrick", "grey30"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = c(8, 1.5), bty = "n")
par(op)
```

## Tiled execution loop

For large destinations, tile the output and call `warp_plan()` + `warp_exec()`
per tile.  This caps memory usage and enables parallel execution:

```{r tiled_loop, eval = FALSE}
tile_size <- 512L
ncol_full <- 4000L; nrow_full <- 3000L

results <- vector("list", ceiling(ncol_full / tile_size) * ceiling(nrow_full / tile_size))
k <- 1L

for (tx in seq(0L, ncol_full - 1L, by = tile_size)) {
  for (ty in seq(0L, nrow_full - 1L, by = tile_size)) {
    tw <- min(tile_size, ncol_full - tx)
    th <- min(tile_size, nrow_full - ty)

    plan_tile <- warp_plan(
      src_crs = src_crs, src_gt = src_gt, src_dim = as.integer(src_dim),
      dst_crs = dst_crs, dst_gt = dst_gt,
      dst_off  = c(tx, ty),
      dst_size = c(tw, th)
    )
    if (is.null(plan_tile)) next

    tile_result <- warp_exec(
      plan_tile, read_fn,
      src_crs, src_gt, dst_crs, dst_gt,
      dst_size = c(tw, th),
      nodata = nodata
    )
    results[[k]] <- list(result = tile_result, xoff = tx, yoff = ty, w = tw, h = th)
    k <- k + 1L
  }
}
```
